it's a double or triple entendre, based on the idiomatic expression "The Stars are Right" (i.e., conditions are favorable, in a mystical sense). Left means opposite of right (in the direction of comedy and the odd), but there is also an idea towards "left" as in remaining. (The Stars are Remaining (but everything else is gone).)

Twenty years ago, between one and four brave wizards saved the world from certain doom at the hands of Assatur -- a terrible daemon from another world. Now, something fishy is stirring in the fishing village of Outsmouth, and I, Vlad, Count of many things, must guide the elderly but still semi-capable wizards once more. All for that most humane of causes: saving the world.

It's not at all a sinister reason, in a couple of hours dusk really does turn to night.

With the giant spider, Parker, lying dead, the wizards made their way through some horribly moist tunnels. As they reached the exit many hours later, it became clear that something sinister was afoot: dusk had turned to night. And if that wasn't enough, they had emerged somewhere familiar, not so far away from the place where they entered the underworld.
